newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Mar 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Mar 20.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- MING PAO -- The Hong Kong Government has decided to rezone 100 hectares of industrial land for residential use to meet housing demands.
-- About 450 kilogrammes of cyanide was spilled into the Pearl River in China's Guangxi province. Hong Kong, Macau and Guangdong province were planning measures to prevent people getting poisoned.

-- WEN WEI PO -- People from all walks of life in Hong Kong have been actively giving their opinion on how to produce the first legislative council of the future Special Administrative Region government.
-- Officials of the People's Bank of China said that interest rates would be kept stable this year, with flexible adjustments when necessary.
-- APPLE DAILY -- The Independent Commission Against Corruption will extend its investigation into alleged syndicated horserace fixing to China and Macau to collect more evidence.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Conservative groups in the United States have started lobbying the White House not to grant China, which they consider "anti-human rights and anti-family values", Most Favoured Nation (MFN) trading status this year.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- The China Securities Regulatory Commission appears to have buckled under intense lobbying pressure from red-chip candidate GITIC Enterprises and other red-chip companies in allowing its listing to proceed.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- China has rejected a People's Liberation Army official's claim that the advance party of military troops from the garrison to be stationed in Hong Kong would not be armed.
